Inline relationships

These study notes describe how an invented research team compares readable article structures. Each sample keeps complete sentences and enough ordinary prose to let article extraction distinguish the main explanation from navigation and unrelated page elements. All people, links, and identifiers in this experiment are fictional.

A strong observation with several words remains part of this sentence, while an emphasized supporting phrase provides a different relationship. The withdrawn suggestion must remain visibly withdrawn. Chemical notation H2O and exponent x2 retain their meaning.

First meaningful line
Second meaningful line after an explicit break.

Literal symbols include *asterisks*, _underscores_, [square brackets], a | pipe, and a backslash \ inside an ordinary sentence.

The researchers review the resulting structure before they compare its presentation. A heading introduces an idea, a list records related observations, and a table relates several values. The comparison must preserve these relationships while using only a detached, sanitized document and without fetching any external resource.
